Article Title: 2003 scandal resurfaces ahead of Uttarakhand polls: What is Harak Singh Rawat-Jenny case
Article Text:
Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma expressed support for Jenny, who is originally from Assam

What are the allegations

How did the controversy first emerge

NEW DELHI: A two-decade-old controversy involving senior Congress leader and former Uttarakhand minister Harak Singh Rawat has resurfaced ahead of the state's assembly elections next year. A woman identified as Jenny has renewed her allegations of rape against Rawat and demanded a fresh DNA test to establish the paternity of her 23-year-old son. The allegations, which first triggered a political storm in 2003, had forced Rawat to resign as a minister before a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe gave him a clean chit in 2004.Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma expressed support for Jenny, who is originally from Assam. After meeting her, Sarma described the alleged treatment she faced as “extremely wrong and reprehensible” and said he stood by her in her fight for justice.Rawat, who currently heads the Congress's election management committee in Uttarakhand, has rejected the renewed allegations, maintained that he was cleared by the CBI and accused the BJP of reviving the controversy for political reasons ahead of the polls.Jenny has claimed that she arrived in Dehradun from Assam in October 2002, when she was 16. She alleged that a party worker took her to Rawat's residence in Yamuna Colony, where she stayed for around one-and-a-half to two months.In an interview with ANI, she accused Rawat of sexually assaulting her and claimed that she subsequently became pregnant. She alleged that she was placed in a Nari Niketan (women's shelter) under the pretext of providing hostel accommodation, where she was kept among people with mental health conditions.At a press conference, Jenny questioned the original investigation, claiming that she was not properly heard by the CBI and was made to sign documents without understanding their contents. She said she had limited knowledge of Hindi at the time and struggled to understand the proceedings.She also questioned the earlier DNA test, asking how it was conducted without collecting blood samples from her or her son.“My son is 23 years old today and has grown up without a father. I do not want anything for myself; I only seek justice for my son. I demand that the CBI re-investigate this case and that a new DNA test be carried out,” she said.Jenny has submitted a written complaint to Uttarakhand DGP Deepam Seth, who forwarded it to the Dehradun SSP for further action. The inquiry has been assigned to Doiwala circle officer Vandana Verma.The case first surfaced in 2003, when Jenny gave birth to a child at a government hospital in Dehradun in June. She alleged that Rawat, then revenue minister in the Congress government led by chief minister Narayan Dutt Tiwari, was the child's father.The allegations triggered a major political storm, forcing Rawat to resign. He also gave up his assembly membership and demanded a CBI investigation, saying he would stay away from public events until his name was cleared.A subsequent CBI investigation and DNA test reportedly found that the child's DNA did not match Rawat's. He was given a clean chit in 2004.Rejecting Jenny's renewed allegations, Rawat said the CBI had already cleared him and the court had closed the matter. He claimed Jenny stayed at his residence for only two days before being sent to a Nari Niketan for her safety.Rawat accused the BJP of using the controversy to divert attention from issues such as the Ankita Bhandari murder case and corruption. He also threatened to file a defamation suit against Dhami, BJP state president Mahendra Bhatt, Jenny and others.
Article Summary: A woman identified as Jenny has renewed her allegations of rape against Harak Singh Rawat. She has demanded a fresh DNA test to establish the paternity of her 23-year-old son. The allegations, which first triggered a political storm in 2003, had forced Rawat to resign as a minister before a CBI probe gave him a clean chit in 2004.

Article Title: 'Things will be known at appropriate time': Sunetra Pawar on NCP merger speculation
Article Text:

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister and Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) president Sunetra Pawar on Wednesday sidestepped a question on the possible merger of the party’s two factions, saying a decision would become clear at the “appropriate time”.“I know all of you are more interested in a different issue at present. However, today’s subject is entirely different. Things (about the merger) will be known when the time comes,” she told reporters in Baramati, the Pawar family’s political stronghold.The NCP, co-founded by veteran politician Sharad Pawar in 1999, split in July 2023 after his nephew, Ajit Pawar , broke away and joined the BJP-led ruling coalition in Maharashtra. The Election Commission subsequently recognised the Ajit Pawar-led faction as the "real" NCP, while the Sharad Pawar-led group was named the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar).In January, the two factions contested the Maharashtra municipal corporation elections in alliance, fuelling speculation about a possible merger. However, Ajit Pawar’s death in a private plane crash later that month cast uncertainty over the prospects of reunification.Speculation about a possible merger gathered momentum last week after several NCP leaders, including Ajit and Sunetra Pawar’s son Parth and senior NCP leader Praful Patel, met Sharad Pawar, who was recently hospitalised with a chest infection.A video that went viral showed Sharad Pawar and Patel discussing a possible meeting after November 10.NCP state president Sunil Tatkare also claimed last week that the merger would have taken place in February if Ajit Pawar had not died.Ajit Pawar, who was Maharashtra’s deputy chief minister and NCP president, died in a private plane crash on January 28. Sunetra Pawar subsequently took over as the party’s president and became deputy chief minister in the BJP-led Maharashtra government, which also includes the Shiv Sena.
Article Summary: NCP split in July 2023 after Ajit Pawar broke away and joined the BJP-led ruling coalition in Maharashtra. In January, the two factions contested the Maharashtra municipal corporation elections in alliance, fuelling speculation about a possible merger. Ajit Pawar’s death in a private plane crash later that month cast uncertainty over the prospects of reunification.

Article Title: Three workers killed during water tank maintenance at Tata iPhone parts factory in Tamil Nadu
Article Text:
Three workers died in an incident at Tata Electronics' facility in Hosur, Tamil Nadu.

NEW DELHI: Three contract workers died on Monday evening after drowning while carrying out maintenance and cleaning work inside a nano-filtration feed tank at Tata Marigold Company in Vanniyapuram, Krishnagiri district, Tamil Nadu The deceased were identified as Kaveri, 28, J Akmal, 28, and Sarath Kumar, 25, all residents of Rayakottai. They were cleaning the tank when the incident occurred.“They were immediately rescued and rushed to a nearby hospital. However, doctors declared them brought dead,” Krishnagiri district collector C Dinesh Kumar said.State minister Virudhai Magal Keerthana expressed grief over the deaths and said she had spoken to the district administration to ensure support for the affected families.“Deeply saddened by the tragic loss of three precious lives in the incident at Tata Electronics' facility in Hosur...I have spoken to the district administration and directed them to extend all necessary support to the affected families and ensure that the situation is addressed with utmost urgency,” she said.“The safety and dignity of every worker must remain paramount. This tragic incident will be thoroughly investigated, and appropriate action will be taken based on the findings.We must ensure that every necessary measure is put in place to prevent such tragedies from recurring,” the minister added.Authorities have launched an inquiry to establish the circumstances leading to the incident and determine whether there were any lapses in industrial safety protocols at the facility. Rayakottai police have registered a case and initiated an investigation. The district administration and police are also monitoring the situation around the industrial unit to maintain law and order.Following an update on the probe from Apple, the company's team visited the Tata factory to investigate the incident, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters.Tata Electronics, an Apple supplier, has also reportedly been instructed to conduct a comprehensive review of the performance and safety compliance of the agencies responsible for maintaining the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP).
Article Summary: Three contract workers died on Monday evening after drowning while carrying out maintenance and cleaning work inside a nano-filtration feed tank at Tata Marigold Company in Vanniyapuram, Krishnagiri district, Tamil Nadu. Authorities have launched an inquiry to establish the circumstances leading to the incident. Apple has also reportedly been instructed to conduct a comprehensive review of the performance and safety compliance of the agencies responsible for maintaining the Effluent Treatment Plant.

Article Title: Hasina seeks passport, Dhaka calls it political stunt & seeks extradition
Article Text:
Kobir said there is no scope now for staging drama in the name of returning to the country using the passport issue (Photo: Reuters).

DHAKA/NEW DELHI: India-Bangladesh ties may experience fresh turbulence with ousted PM Sheikh Hasina 's legal counsel formally requesting a new passport and national identity card from the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi to facilitate her return to the country. While the high commission said it wasn't sure if the request was genuine as it was not backed by supporting documents, Dhaka responded by declaring it doesn't issue passports to "convicted terrorists" and reiterating its demand for Hasina's extradition.India, however, sees the passport request as a matter purely between the government in Dhaka and a Bangladeshi national, one that should not be conflated with her extradition issue. The Indian government maintains that Hasina's extradition is subject to established legal and judicial processes under the bilateral extradition treaty.Hasina had earlier announced that she planned to 'return' to Bangladesh in December. However, India is likely to distance itself from Hasina's passport bid - described by Bangladesh authorities as a political stunt - as it believes this will be Dhaka's call entirely."She has fled after killing people. One who has fled, how would she come? How would a terrorist come? There’s an extradition treaty. Handover would be sought through the treaty," said Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Humaiun Kobir.Kobir said there is no scope now for staging drama in the name of returning to the country using the passport issue.“If she truly wishes to return, there is a specific legal process for doing so. An extradition treaty exists between Bangladesh and India; she should ask the Indian government to hand her over to Bangladesh under the terms of that treaty. She should return, surrender to the court, and serve her sentence,” he said.Political insiders in Dhaka say the government and opposition party Jamaat do not actually want Hasina’s return at this moment and that is why the government is unwilling to accept her voluntary return and tagging extradition treaty issue which is time-consuming and complicated.In 2025, a Bangladeshi special tribunal sentenced her to death for crimes against humanity, ruling that she was responsible for ordering the crackdown, which left hundreds of people dead and thousands of others injured.Hasina requested a new passport on Monday to facilitate her return from exile two years after she was ousted in a mass uprising.In a letter, emailed to the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, Hasina’s counsel urged the top diplomat to take necessary action to provide her with a passport and national identity card.The letter, sent by London-based law firm Matrix Chambers, asked the mission for the application to be processed “expeditiously” on the basis of Hasina’s Bangladeshi nationality and in accordance with “obligations arising under international human rights instruments.”The letter, sent via email and addressed to Acting High Commissioner Preeti Rahman, was shared with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.Hasina’s application is ridiculous, State Minister Kobir said, criticising the British law firm over its involvement in the matter.“Know your client. Don’t run after her looted money from the people of Bangladesh. Exercise some ethical and moral boundaries. And if you don’t have those boundaries, you will be shamed all over the world,” he said.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina told AP in response to questions by email. “So, I will return to Bangladesh. That decision has not changed.”
Article Summary: Ousted PM Sheikh Hasina's legal counsel formally requested a new passport and national identity card from the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi. Dhaka responded by declaring it doesn't issue passports to "convicted terrorists" India, however, sees the passport request as a matter purely between the government in Dhaka and a Bangladeshi national.

Article Title: Ahead of peace talks, Zelenskyy seeks PM Modi's help on ceasefire
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi and Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke Monday

NEW DELHI: Ahead of the Abu Dhabi peace talks, PM Narendra Modi and Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke Monday with the latter briefing the PM about latest developments related to the Russia-Ukraine conflict and Modi conveying India’s "firm commitment" to contributing in every possible way towards a peaceful resolution of the Russia-Ukraine war.The conversation took place a day before the trilateral peace dialogue involving Russia, Ukraine and the US in Abu Dhabi, and amid renewed Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure. Ahead of the talks, where India's recent peace proposals are likely to be discussed too, India remained engaged with both sides on diplomatic initiatives as foreign minister S Jaishankar too spoke to his Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov.Zelenskyy recalled Modi's latest peace message to President Vladimir Putin that it was time now to end the "endless war" and urged India to take more steps towards a ceasefire that can ensure food and energy security. Modi said in a post on X that he and Zelenskyy had a productive conversation – their first since they met on the margins of the G7 summit in France in June.Modi's message to Zelenskyy expressing India's readiness to facilitate peace is not new, but its timing is significant as this was the first time they spoke after Jaishankar revealed in early October India was actively mediating for establishment of safe corridors in the Black Sea for grain and energy exports."We reviewed our wide-ranging bilateral cooperation and agreed to further strengthen India-Ukraine ties. I thanked President Zelenskyy for sharing his perspectives on the ongoing conflict, its humanitarian aspects and various efforts to restore peace," said Modi in his own readout of the talks.Ukraine believes Russia has not responded positively to India's Black Sea shipping proposal and the call to end targeting of its energy sector. "The Prime Minister has said more than once, including directly to the Russian ‌leader, ⁠that now is the time to end the war, not to continue it," said Zelenskyy on X after his talks with Modi, urging India to identify steps it can take and also talks it can pursue with other leaders to bring the conflict to an end.“Food security could be one such area. We discussed Russia's blocking of grain exports via the Black Sea. India is ready to mediate in establishing food corridors, and we are counting on these efforts to continue,” said the Ukrainian president.Zelenskyy also said Ukraine had always taken a constructive approach, and Russia must show the same readiness to de-escalate.“Russia must understand that the global economy and hundreds of millions of people around the world are suffering because of blocked sea routes. We agreed that our teams will stay in touch on these and other bilateral issues,” he said.An Indian readout said Modi reaffirmed India’s human-centric approach and reiterated India’s consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy.The 4th round of Russia-Ukraine peace talks mediated by the US are scheduled to begin in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. While the core negotiations are structured as trilateral sessions involving Russia, Ukraine, and the US, Ukrainian delegation will hold separate coordination meetings with their European and Nato allies including France, Germany and the UK on the sidelines.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi and Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke Monday ahead of the Abu Dhabi peace talks. The conversation took place a day before the trilateral peace dialogue involving Russia, Ukraine and the US in Abu Dhabi. India's recent peace proposals are likely to be discussed too.

Article Title: 'Next target is to finish Dimagi Naxals': Kiren Rijiju slams Rahul Gandhi for attacking PM Modi
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Tuesday slammed Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi for attacking Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks on 'Dimagi Naxal'.In a social media post on X, Rijiju reminded Rahul that former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh had described Left-wing extremism as the biggest internal security threat to the country."Rahul ji, thank Modi ji for eliminating the Armed Maoists. Former PM Dr Manmohan Singh ji had famously described Left-Wing Extremism and Naxalism as 'The single biggest internal security threat' to India," Rijiju said."Next target is to finish Dimagi Naxals," he added.This comes a day after Rahul hit back at PM Modi over his 'Dimagi Naxal' remarks, claiming that the CRPF jawans' facial expressions suggested they did not believe the Prime Minister's claims.In a post on X addressed to CRPF personnel who attended PM Modi's Diwali event in Bastar, Rahul said, "Your faces said it all: you didn't buy the PM's lies. He called us Naxals.""My challenge stands. Let him debate me on who is anti-national and who is controlled by foreign forces. Any time, any place," he said, adding, "My guarantee: after the debate, the PM won't have the guts to stand in front of a single jawan again."The war of words began after PM Modi, while celebrating Diwali with security personnel in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, said that although armed Naxalites had been wiped out from forests, "Dimagi Naxals" had infiltrated several organisations and political parties and were inciting people against the Constitution and democracy.The Prime Minister also accused previous governments of restricting the freedom of security personnel engaged in anti-Naxal operations, saying his government had given them the authority to take necessary decisions."We must remember one thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not yet over. While armed Naxalites have been wiped out from the forests, 'Dimagi Naxals' have taken control of several organisations. Even today, they are inciting people against the country's Constitution and democracy. These 'Dimagi Naxals' have also infiltrated several political parties and different organisations. We must identify them, defeat them and ensure the security of the nation," PM Modi said.The remarks came months after the Centre announced on March 31 that the country had been freed from the menace of Naxalism, following the elimination of several Maoist leaders and cadres and the surrender of hundreds of others.
Article Summary: Rijiju reminded Rahul that former PM Manmohan Singh had described Left-wing extremism as the biggest internal security threat to the country. Rahul hit back at PM Modi over his 'Dimagi Naxal' remarks, claiming that the CRPF jawans' facial expressions suggested they did not believe the Prime Minister's claims.

Article Title: MEA slams US court summons to Doval, RAW ex-chief Goel
Article Text:
MEA slams US court summons to Doval, RAW ex-chief Goel

Summons served by US court said to be ‘routine, procedural step’

New Delhi: Govt on Tuesday dismissed a US court civil summons naming national security adviser Ajit Doval and former R&AW chief Samant Goel as a "frivolous lawsuit" driven by "fabricated and malicious" claims, asserting that designated Khalistani terrorist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun's legal maneuvering did not hold any merit, reports Rajshekhar Jha."...Requests for the service of judicial documents in India can only be routed through India's designated central authority, that is, the ministry of law and justice," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.MEA's reaction came on reports of the US state department notifying India via a diplomatic note about a civil suit filed by SFJ member Pannun regarding an alleged plot to assassinate him.The summons naming Doval and Goel among the defendants seeks damages for an attempt on Pannun’s life and was delivered to the Indian embassy in Washington on Oct 9. Sources described the move as a “routine, procedural step”. They said this was not the first time such a summons had been served by US courts.Former PM Manmohan Singh was served with a civil summons in 2013 in connection with a suit filed by the same outfit, SFJ, alleging human rights violations related to 1984. In 2013, a federal court in Washington DC had issued summons to Singh during his visit to Washington. Former Chinese President Jiang Zemin was also served a similar summons in 2002.Both suits were eventually dismissed.The court order in the Pannun case came ahead of the Nov 20 sentencing of Nikhil Gupta, an Indian national arrested by the US in the matter.The state department note also clarified that the action was carried out in compliance with court instructions and does not indicate any US position on the case.“The performance of state department of its statutory functions under 28 USC (US Codes). 1608 should not be construed as an indication in any way of the US’s’ position or views on whether plaintiffs have properly complied with all statutory requirements of the FSIA (Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act), the status or character of a defendant, whether service was properly effected, or the merits of any claims or defenses,” it said.
Article Summary: MEA slams US court summons to Doval, RAW ex-chief Goel as a 'frivolous lawsuit' The summons was delivered to the Indian embassy in Washington on Oct 9. Sources described the move as a ‘routine, procedural step’

Article Title: 'Unfortunate': Govt condemns anti-India campaign by Chinese vloggers, urges Bangladesh to take action
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Tuesday condemned an alleged coordinated anti-India campaign by Chinese nationals who have reportedly been filming videos in slum areas of Dhaka for months and portraying the locations as parts of New Delhi during livestreams on Chinese social media platforms.During the weekly press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal termed the incident as "unfortunate" and said that attempts to project a distorted picture of a country only undermine the credibility of those involved and those backing them."We have seen media reports in this regard. Such efforts to present a distorted picture of any country are unfortunate," Jaiswal said."Insofar as efforts to buy foreign elements to portray Dhaka as Delhi are concerned, the peddling of false narratives only undermines the credibility of those who are undertaking such actions and those who are behind them. And I would urge the authorities concerned to take action against such people," he added.According to recent media reports, Chinese vloggers and livestreamers have been recording videos in impoverished neighbourhoods of Dhaka, Bangladesh, while falsely identifying the locations as parts of New Delhi.The videos reportedly feature derogatory remarks about India's living conditions, sanitation, food habits and poverty.According to Prothom Alo, the activity has been reported in Sector 12 of Uttara and the adjoining Tekpara area of Dhaka, where local residents estimate that more than 150 Chinese nationals have been recording videos.The vloggers reportedly walk through streets and alleyways carrying two mobile phones, livestreaming for hours and, at times, entering people's homes to film. Their activities, which have continued for months, have increasingly angered residents, who remain unaware of where the footage is being published and how it is being presented.A Chinese national identified as Fangyou told Prothom Alo that the livestreams were part of product promotion activities on WeChat. A Bangladeshi woman, Ritu Akhter, who works as a guide for the Chinese nationals, said they also earned money by posting videos on platforms such as Douyin, the Chinese version of TikTok."This is New Delhi. Their homes are extremely dirty. There isn't even a fan inside the tin-roofed houses. This place is quite underdeveloped, dirty and unhygienic, and the law-and-order situation is poor," she said.Apart from the misleading portrayal of their neighbourhoods, residents have raised concerns over repeated filming and alleged intrusions into their homes. Some claimed that the Chinese nationals entered houses and even bathrooms while recording."Sometimes they enter our homes and start filming. We are not always properly dressed inside our houses. Imagine how it feels when someone suddenly walks into your home and starts recording," resident Rozina Khatun told Prothom Alo.
Article Summary: Chinese vloggers and livestreamers have been recording videos in impoverished neighbourhoods of Dhaka, Bangladesh, while falsely identifying the locations as parts of New Delhi. The videos reportedly feature derogatory remarks about India's living conditions, sanitation, food habits and poverty. Residents have raised concerns over repeated filming and alleged intrusions into their homes.

Article Title: 2008 CRPF camp attack convict shot dead by unknown gunman in UP
Article Text:
Sharif was killed in Rampur with bystanders alleging he was shot 16 times

NEW DELHI: An unknown gunman shot dead Mohammad Sharif , an accused linked to the 2008 CRPF camp attack, on Tuesday. Sharif was killed in Rampur, UP with bystanders alleging he was shot 16 times. The police have initiated a manhunt for the shooter/s.Seven CRPF personnel and a rickshaw puller were killed in a pre-dawn terror attack, plotted by Lashkar-e-Taiba , on the CRPF Group Centre in Rampur on the night of December 31, 2007-Jan 1, 2008. In May 2025, unknown gunmen had killed Abu Saifullah Khalid, a key Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) operative and the mastermind behind the 2006 RSS headquarters attack and multiple terror strikes, including one on a CRPF camp in Uttar Pradesh.Sharif, who belonged to Badanpuri-Khajuria village in Rampur, went by aliases of Suhail, Sajid, Anwar and Ali, according to police records. He was lodged in Bareilly central jail and released last Nov.Arrested in the case in the aftermath of the attack, a UP court had in 2019 convicted Sharif and five others including two Pakistani nationals in the case. Four including Sharif were subsequently sentenced to death after they were found directly involved in the attack.In Oct 2025, the Allahabad High Court, however, overturned the death sentences but upheld their conviction under the Arms Act for possessing prohibited weapons, sentencing them to ten years’ rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs 1 lakh each. The HC had noted procedural lapses by the police like failure to conduct a Test Identification Parade (TIP) and also found lapses in the handling of physical evidence, observing that firearms, cartridges, and grenades allegedly recovered from the scene were not securely preserved or properly traced through the chain of custody. Key witnesses who should have verified storage and transfer of evidence were not examined.
Article Summary: Sharif was killed in Rampur, UP with bystanders alleging he was shot 16 times. The police have initiated a manhunt for the shooter/s. Seven CRPF personnel and a rickshaw puller were killed in a pre-dawn terror attack, plotted by Lashkar-e- Taiba.

Article Text:

Article Title: ‘Stolen donations, betrayed faith’: Congress seeks SC-monitored probe against BJP, RSS over Ram Temple funds
Article Text:
Ramesh questions BJP, RSS role in Ram Temple donation case

Ramesh cites earlier complaints, questions role of trust officials

Congress questions PM Modi, Adityanath over trust and investigation

SIT chargesheet names eight accused in donation case

Congress demands public disclosure of financial records

NEW DELHI: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh on Wednesday questioned the alleged links of people accused in the Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation embezzlement case with the BJP, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) and Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP), accusing the organisations of evading responsibility despite their members being involved in the temple's construction and management.In a post on X, Ramesh alleged that people associated with the BJP, RSS and VHP were in charge of the temple trust, construction work, donation collection, counting of offerings and their deposit in banks.He demanded that the investigation be widened beyond the eight employees arrested in the case and that the role of everyone responsible for the temple's functioning be examined under the Supreme Court's supervision.“Stolen donations, betrayed faith,” Ramesh wrote, adding that those who oversaw the different stages of the donation process “cannot shirk responsibility for the theft of offerings”.The Congress leader also called for the publication of all financial records and a complete account of donations and offerings received at the temple in the name of Lord Ram.Ramesh referred to allegations made in 2021 by Mahipal Singh, a former accounts officer associated with the RSS who was sent to the temple to serve.According to the Congress leader, Singh had detected alleged irregularities in the handling of offerings and reported them to temple trust officials Champat Rai and Gopal Rao.Ramesh alleged that Singh was removed instead of action being taken against those responsible. He questioned why Rai and Gopal Rao were witnesses rather than accused in the chargesheet, given the earlier complaints.He also cited media reports about Deenanath Verma, the engineer overseeing construction, who allegedly claimed that a 40 per cent commission was demanded for work at the trust office. Verma reportedly played an audio recording of the alleged demand to Rai, after which he was removed from the project, Ramesh said.The Congress leader questioned whether Rai had been directly questioned over the allegation.Ramesh further referred to reported organisational links of some of the accused. He alleged that Anukalp Mishra had links with the Bajrang Dal and an RSS shakha, and said Rai had attended Mishra's Bhagwat Katha on April 30, 2026.He also cited media reports that Subhash Srivastava, who was in charge of the counting staff, used to run an RSS shakha at his home. The SIT has reportedly held Srivastava responsible for handing over the keys to donation boxes to unauthorised people. Ramesh also alleged that another accused, Tinnu Yadav, had worked as Rai's driver.Questioning the recruitment process, Ramesh said advertisements were issued and selection and training committees formed for the appointment of priests, but there was no advertisement or interview process for staff in the room where donations worth crores of rupees were counted every week. He asked why those who allegedly appointed their associates had not been named as accused.Ramesh also questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath over their response to the allegations.He recalled that PM Modi had announced the formation of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust in the Lok Sabha on February 5, 2020. Ramesh alleged that the process had been handled personally by the prime minister and that details of the selection criteria and deliberations had not been made public.He asked why the prime minister and chief minister, whom he accused of seeking credit for the temple, had remained silent over the alleged theft of donations.The Congress leader also questioned the handling of the Special Investigation Team's findings. Referring to Adityanath's statement in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly that the government had formed the SIT following a request from the trust, Ramesh asked whether the first report had been handed to the same trust whose office-bearers were facing allegations of corruption.He demanded that the report be made public, questioning why it remained undisclosed if it had been shared with people facing allegations.“The biggest question is why all the suspects and accused have links only to the BJP, RSS and Vishva Hindu Parishad?” he wrote.The allegations come after the SIT filed a nearly 70,000-page chargesheet against eight arrested people in the temple donation embezzlement case.The chargesheet names Avinash Shukla, Anukalp Mishra, Lavkush Mishra, Manish Yadav, Karunesh Pandey, Ramashankar Mishra, Subhash Srivastava and Ram Shankar Yadav alias Tinnu. The case was registered in June after the preliminary investigation flagged suspected diversion of temple donations.The SIT reportedly identified 105 instances of unauthorised removal or concealment of cash during the counting process inside the temple premises. Investigators recovered Rs 79.85 lakh in cash allegedly linked to the embezzlement from the accused, except Srivastava.The chargesheet includes allegations of criminal breach of trust and offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act. It contains statements from nearly 190 witnesses, banking records, property details, asset trails and findings from a forensic audit.The SIT also examined the movement of donations from collection boxes and counters to bank deposits. Investigators found evidence of cash being siphoned off during counting but no signs of pilferage during its transfer to banks.Ramesh said accountability should not be confined to the eight employees arrested in the case. He called for an investigation into everyone involved in the temple's construction, management and donation-handling system, under the supervision of the Supreme Court.“The Congress demands that all financial records be made public, the scope of the investigation be expanded and everyone found guilty be dealt with according to the law,” he wrote.“The country must be given a full accounting of the donations and offerings received in the name of Lord Shri Ram. No position, political access or organisational protection can shield anyone from accountability.”The donation case has also drawn criticism from Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. In an X post on Tuesday, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister said his party would seek to restore Ayodhya's dignity through transparent management if it came to power in the 2027 Assembly elections.Yadav alleged that the donation theft had hurt devotees' faith and affected the number of pilgrims visiting the temple town, with consequences for Ayodhya's local economy. He also promised better infrastructure, religious tourism facilities and greater opportunities for local contractors and residents.
Article Summary: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh questions alleged links of people accused in the Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation embezzlement case. He accuses the BJP, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) and Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) of evading responsibility. He demands that the investigation be widened beyond the eight employees arrested in the case.

Article Title: 'This is not UCC, but Hindu Civil Code': Owaisi targets Maharashtra govt, says move seeks to 'snatch' Muslims' identity
Article Text:
Owaisi says in Islam, 'Nikah is a contract, not a lifelong bond.'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi on Tuesday slammed the Maharashtra government's proposed Uniform Civil Code (UCC), alleging that it was aimed at targeting Muslims and imposing a "Hindu Civil Code" on non-Hindu communities.Questioning the government's approach, Owaisi asked, "Why accept tribal customs but not Muslim practices?" He alleged that the proposed code would restrict Muslims from following their religious practices, particularly those related to marriage and divorce."This UCC is being brought to stop Muslims from practising their religion. In Islam, marriage is a contract. You are also imposing divorce rules as per the Hindu Marriage Act. All this is being done to target Muslims and snatch their identity," he said, ANI reported.Owaisi said Nikah was an essential part of marriage under Islam and argued that different religions followed distinct personal laws adding that, "In Islam, marriage is called nikah. It is not a religious ritual. Nikah is a contract, not a lifelong bond."If there is no nikah, then what is it? If a child is born out of a relationship, does that make it a marriage? No, it is not a marriage, he said.He also argued that the UCC would give legal rights to children born out of live-in relationships, which he said was not permitted under Islamic religious practices.Owaisi made the remarks at a press conference after the Mahayuti government invited public suggestions on implementing the UCC in Maharashtra and released a questionnaire for the consultation.He claimed the questionnaire indicated that the Devendra Fadnavis-led government had already decided to implement the code."The subject of the press conference today is that the Maharashtra Government has invited opinions from the public to implement UCC. The state government has also prepared a questionnaire for it. This questionnaire, prepared by the Maharashtra government, makes it clear that the Devendra Fadnavis govt will implement the UCC," he said.Owaisi questioned the questionnaire's focus on polygamy and extra-judicial divorce, alleging that it did not address the Hindu Undivided Family (HUF)."The questionnaire consists of leading questions on polygamy and extra-judicial divorce. But there is not one question on Hindu Undivided Family," he said.He compared the proposed exercise with UCC initiatives undertaken by BJP governments in Gujarat, Uttarakhand, Assam and Madhya Pradesh, claiming that these were attempts to impose a "Hindu Civil Code" on non-Hindu communities."This makes it evident that, much like the initiatives introduced by BJP governments in Gujarat, Uttarakhand, Assam, and Madhya Pradesh under the guise of a 'Uniform Civil Code,' this is not a true UCC, but rather a 'Hindu Civil Code' that is being imposed upon non-Hindu communities," Owaisi said.He also objected to the format of the questionnaire, saying most of its questions were framed to elicit yes-or-no responses."Additionally, if you examine the questionnaire, you will find that the majority of the questions are framed in a 'yes or no' format," he added.Owaisi also linked the resignation of retired Bombay High court judge RC Chavan to the composition of the exercise. He said Chavan had cited the absence of a member from the minority community as a reason for stepping down."I believe this is precisely why RC Chavan, a retired judge of the Bombay HC, chose to resign. He had stated that there is no one from the minority community," he said."They are talking about implementation in the state of Maharashtra at this juncture, but they are not defining what this 'uniform' actually is," he added.Meanwhile, Maharashtra Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis defended his government's decision to draft a UCC, saying the Constitution directs states to work towards its implementation. Hitting back at Owaisi, Fadnavis said the UCC was rooted in the Directive Principles of State Policy.
Article Summary: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi slams Maharashtra government's proposed Uniform Civil Code (UCC) He alleges that it was aimed at targeting Muslims and imposing a "Hindu Civil Code" on non-Hindu communities. Maharashtra Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis defends his government's decision to draft a UCC.

Article Title: Sonia Gandhi memoir: BJP's Phoolka questions Army timeline, Indira's tears on 1984 riots
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: BJP leader and senior advocate HS Phoolka has challenged Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's account of the 1984 anti-Sikh violence and Operation Blue Star in her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, alleging that some of the details contradict official records and historical documents.He has questioned her account of when the Army was called in following Indira Gandhi's assassination and also disputed her description of the former prime minister's emotional reaction to Operation Blue Star.Speaking to news agency ANI, Phoolka said he had received several calls from media organisations seeking his response to Sonia Gandhi's account that the Army was called in on October 31, 1984, the day then prime minister Indira Gandhi was assassinated."I got several phone calls from media. They said Sonia Gandhi has written that during the 1984 Sikh massacre, the Army was called on 31st October itself. I have purchased the book to read whether this is indeed written in the book. If this is written in the book, it is against the records. It is absolutely false," Phoolka told ANI.Referring to the Misra Commission's findings, Phoolka maintained that the Army was formally called in only on the evening of November 1 and reached the affected areas in significant numbers on November 2.Phoolka also cited the commission's observations on the availability of Army personnel in Delhi during the violence."Misra Commission stated that 5,000 Army personnel were available within Delhi and they were not deployed. Misra Commission stated that had they been deployed, lives of 2,000 Sikhs could have been saved," he said.The Misra Commission found that an additional Army brigade of around 1,600 personnel had reached Delhi from Meerut before midnight on October 31, 1984.However, the Delhi administration delayed formally requisitioning Army assistance. The Army became operational in parts of central and south Delhi by the evening of November 1, while five additional brigades arrived on November 2. The commission observed that deploying around 5,000 available Army personnel on the morning of November 1 could have prevented at least 2,000 deaths."Phoolka also questioned Sonia Gandhi's account of Indira Gandhi's alleged remorse following Operation Blue Star, the military operation carried out at the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar in June 1984.In her memoir, Sonia Gandhi reportedly recounts seeing Indira Gandhi watching a slow-motion recording of the operation's aftermath, with tears in her eyes. She describes the former prime minister's emotional reaction as an expression of pain and regret over the loss of lives during the operation.Disputing this account, Phoolka said it did not appear to be consistent with the historical record. He referred to a fact-finding report prepared by a team led by former Supreme Court judge Justice VM Tarkunde in September 1984, which he said included postmortem reports documenting the aftermath of the military operation."This doesn't seem to be true. In September, Justice Tarkunde's team wrote a fact-finding report on Operation Blue Star. Actual postmortem report was included in the report. The entire team was arrested and the report was banned," he told ANI.Questioning the account of Indira Gandhi's remorse, Phoolka further said, "If you look at the actual facts, you won't find any regrets or tears. It might be crocodile tears."
Article Summary: HS Phoolka has challenged Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's account of 1984 anti- Sikh violence and Operation Blue Star in her memoir. He has questioned her account of when the Army was called in following Indira Gandhi's assassination and also disputed her description of the former prime minister's emotional reaction to the operation. He said the Misra Commission's findings on the availability of Army personnel in Delhi during the violence did not seem to be true.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Tuesday extended the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) restrictions to retired public officials engaged or re-employed by state governments in five states scheduled to hold assembly elections next year.In a letter to the chief secretaries and chief electoral officers of Goa, Manipur, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, the commission said such officials must maintain political neutrality and refrain from participating in election campaigns or canvassing for political parties or candidates."The Commission has in the past, in respect of the conduct of government employees, issued instructions stating that they are not expected to take part in any election campaign or canvassing and should take scrupulous care not to lend their names, official position or authority to assist one individual/political party/group as against another," the letter said.The commission noted that several retired government officials and employees are engaged, attached, employed or re-employed by state and Union Territory governments in various capacities, but there are no specific rules or guidelines governing their political neutrality and conduct during the MCC period.Assembly elections are due in all five states in 2027, with polling expected in February-March. The terms of the Goa, Manipur, Punjab and Uttarakhand assemblies end in March, while the Uttar Pradesh Assembly's term expires in May.
Article Summary: Election Commission extends Model Code of Conduct restrictions to retired public officials. Officials in five states scheduled to hold assembly elections next year must maintain political neutrality. Goa, Manipur, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand to hold elections in 2027.

Article Title: 1 year of Delhi blast: Al-Falah university, where module operated, fills all MBBS seats
Article Text:
Al-Falah University has filled its 200 MBBS seats, driven by a comprehensive governance reform





GURGAON: A year after the blast near Red Fort metro station claimed 15 lives and revealed a terrorist module being run by a group of doctors at Faridabad ’s Al-Falah University, its medical college has seen a reversal in fortunes.Now being run by a govt administrator, with the founder in prison, the college has filled all its 200 MBBS seats in the latest admission cycle, emerging from uncertainty about its future after intense scrutiny of its staff as well as students by investigating agencies.Academic activities have returned to normal at Al-Falah, with its affairs now directly under state govt’s watch following its takeover in March 2026. MBBS seats in the state are allotted through centralised counselling by Pt Bhagwat Dayal Sharma University of Health Sciences in Rohtak.IAS officer Amit Kumar Aggrawal was appointed administrator on March 21 this year. A team from JC Bose University of Science and Technology in Faridabad also took key posts.Ajay Ranga, registrar at JC Bose University, was given additional charge as Al-Falah’s vice-chancellor.Rajeev Kumar Singh, controller of examinations at JC Bose, was assigned the same role at Al-Falah, while Ravi Kumar Sharma was appointed chief finance and accounts officer and Meha Sharma was appointed registrar.Al-Falah founder-chairperson Jawad Ahmed Siddiqui was arrested in two separate cases of money laundering.An official credited the university’s turnaround to several measures taken after an inquiry found multiple statutory violations and irregularities in the functioning of the university.“The university now has around 80% of its faculty positions through advertisements in newspapers. Faculty members were earlier paid different salaries. The university now has introduced a uniform and improved salary structure, which has helped attract good professors,” said an official who is part of the govt-appointed administrative setup.“Before the incident, the university had faculty members who were associated with private clinics but were also registered as professors here but not actually teaching. They were paid for their association with Al-Falah. All such bogus faculty members have been removed. There is strict biometric attendance system now in place,” the official added. In the previous admission cycle, the university had filled 196 of its 200 seats.Al-Falah became the focus of an investigation by National Investigation Agency (NIA) after Dr Umer Un Nabi, who allegedly drove the i20 that blew up near Red Fort last Nov, was found to have worked there as an assistant professor.The agency’s chargesheet also alleged that Umer, his colleague Dr Muzammil Shakeel Ganaie and Dr Adeel Ahmed Rather tested explosives and firearms in villages in the vicinity, while Dr Shaheen Shahid helped finance weapons.According to NIA, the explosives were tested near a campus tubewell before trials shifted to fields and the Aravalis.Although the university denied any involvement of the institution as a whole, the investigation led to concerns among students that the college would shut down.The new administration also ordered fresh police checks of all students, employees and stakeholders, including those with incomplete records.“Everyone was scrutinised, every employee, every student and every stakeholder. We have re-verified everyone associated with the university. For those whose police verification reports were not available in our records, we have submitted their details again,” an official said.The official said no foreign student is currently enrolled at Al-Falah. A few from Dubai and Nepal had studied there earlier.“Yes, Al-Falah was at the centre of a terror investigation after the blast last year. But whatever inquiry is being conducted is being handled by respective agencies. The administration has no role in the probe,” the official said.
Article Summary: Al-Falah University has filled all its 200 MBBS seats in the latest admission cycle. The college has emerged from uncertainty about its future after intense scrutiny of its staff as well as students by investigating agencies. The university is now directly under state govt’s watch following its takeover in March 2026.

Article Title: 'Injured his own throat with scissors': New twist in Kolkata techie Sarthak Sarkar's murder case; girlfriend gives contradictory accounts
Article Text:

Contradictory accounts complicate investigation

Argument over alleged relationships before murder

Neighbours heard screams, found man lying in blood

KOLKATA: The investigation into the murder of 25-year-old software engineer Sarthak Sarkar in Kolkata remains inconclusive, with police yet to establish what was used to inflict the fatal injury to his throat and who delivered the blow.Investigators are examining whether a thin, pointed object, possibly a chopstick, was used in the attack. They are also trying to reconstruct the sequence of events inside the rented flat in Fartabad, Garia, where Sarkar was found critically injured late on Saturday night.Sarkar's live-in partner, Sanchalika Basu (22), and her mother, Moumita Basu, have been arrested in connection with the murder. However, police have not been able to establish a clear account of what happened, despite questioning the two women in custody.According to police, the mother and daughter have given contradictory statements during interrogation.Sanchalika allegedly told investigators at one point that Sarkar had injured his own throat with a pair of scissors. On another occasion, she reportedly said she could not remember what had happened during the heated argument.Investigators are trying to verify these claims and determine whether scissors or another sharp object was used in the attack.Police also suspect that Sarkar was assaulted during an argument with Sanchalika. They are examining the exact circumstances in which Moumita entered the room and whether she had any role in the attack.The couple had reportedly been quarrelling for some time over allegations of extramarital relationships.On Saturday night, an argument allegedly broke out between them while they were drinking. Both reportedly accused each other of being involved with multiple partners.Investigators suspect that the confrontation turned violent, leaving Sarkar with a fatal injury. However, the precise sequence of events and the role played by each of the two arrested women remain unclear.Sarkar, a resident of Barasat, had been living in the rented flat at Fartabad with Sanchalika. Her mother, Moumita, also stayed with them.Residents said they were alerted to the incident around 1.30 am when a woman ran out of the flat, crying and seeking help.“We were still awake when we heard a woman crying and asking for help. We immediately rushed to the flat and found a young man lying in a pool of blood on the bed. The woman who had sought our help had several scratch marks on her neck. We immediately informed the police,” said Sayan Pal, a Garia resident.He added that some occupants of the same building had heard a heated argument and loud noises coming from the flat shortly before the incident.Another local resident, Arkojeet Basu, said the couple had been living in the area for some time but rarely interacted with neighbours.“They did not mix much with people in the neighbourhood. We were shocked to learn about the incident in the morning,” he said.Sarkar was rushed to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Police are continuing to question the arrested women and examine the evidence to establish how the attack took place.
Article Summary: Sarkar's live-in partner, Sanchalika Basu (22), and her mother, Moumita Basu, have been arrested. Police have not been able to establish a clear account of what happened, despite questioning the two women in custody.

Article Title: Woman killed with brick after argument with Facebook friend in Ghaziabad’s Loni
Article Text:
The deceased has been identified as Pinky, a native of Bulandshahr





GHAZIABAD: A woman was allegedly killed by a man she had befriended on Facebook around four to five months ago following an argument during their meeting in Ghaziabad’s Loni Border area on Monday.The deceased has been identified as Pinky, a native of Bulandshahr, while the accused, identified as Pintu, also hails from the same district.According to police, the incident came to light on Monday when the Indrapuri police outpost, under the Loni Border police station, received information about the murder of a woman. A police team, accompanied by senior officers, immediately reached the spot and inspected the crime scene.During preliminary inquiries, police discovered that Pinky and Pintu had come into contact through Facebook approximately four to five months ago. They subsequently began communicating over phone calls and developed a friendship.On Monday, Pintu reportedly visited Pinky to meet her. However, an argument broke out between them over an issue that is yet to be established.Police said the altercation escalated when Pintu allegedly picked up a brick lying nearby and struck Pinky on the head, causing fatal injuries.ACP Ankur Vihar Amardeep Maurya said the woman's body was taken into custody and sent for post-mortem examination after completing the necessary legal formalities."The two had become friends through Facebook around four to five months ago. The accused visited the woman on Monday, and an argument broke out between them. He allegedly attacked her on the head with a brick, resulting in her death," Maurya said.Police are questioning the accused to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the incident and the motive behind the alleged attack.Further legal proceedings are underway, while investigators are examining the sequence of events that led to the woman's death.
Article Summary: The deceased has been identified as Pinky, a native of Bulandshahr. The accused, identified as Pintu, also hails from the same district. The two had become friends through Facebook around four to five months ago.

Article Title: 1 killed as UP village head opens fire over gambling dispute; surrenders fearing encounter
Article Text:
Bakrabad village head Sanjay Bind, 40





VARANASI: One person was killed while another suffered a bullet injury after Bakrabad village head Sanjay Bind, 40, allegedly opened fire on them during a dispute over gambling in Mohav village under Kotwali police station limits in Ghazipur district late Monday night.Police teams began raiding possible hideouts of Bind, but he managed to reach Kotwali police station on Tuesday afternoon and surrendered before the police.Ghazipur ASP (City) Rakesh Kumar Mishra said around 10 people were gambling near a pond at Pasipurwa in Mohav village on Monday night. Around 10.30 pm, Bind and his associates joined them. Witnesses told police that after an argument broke out, Bind pulled out a pistol and opened indiscriminate fire.The bullets hit Ajay Pasi, 28, of Mohav, and Surendra Ram, 35, of Islamabad village, while Bind managed to escape. Both injured men were rushed to Ghazipur Medical College. However, doctors found their condition critical and referred them to the trauma centre at BHU in Varanasi. Ajay died during treatment, while Surendra, a mason, remained under treatment.On receiving information, Ghazipur SP Vinay Kumar Singh, Mishra and other officials reached the spot and also met the injured men at the hospital.Later, several teams were deployed to arrest Bind.However, fearing a police encounter, Bind reached Kotwali police station carrying a placard stating that he was surrendering and turned himself in on Tuesday afternoon. He told the police that he had won Rs 1.5 lakh while gambling and that others tried to snatch the money, leading to the firing.Police said Bind has several previous cases registered against him, including one for attacking a police team during Holi celebrations. He has two other criminal cases against him. Following the Holi incident, he was arrested and sent to jail. He was recently granted bail by the High Court and released from jail.
Article Summary: Bakarabad village head Sanjay Bind, 40, allegedly opened fire on them during a dispute over gambling. Ajay Pasi, 28, died during treatment, while Surendra Ram, 35, remained under treatment. Bind has several previous cases registered against him, including one for attacking a police team during Holi celebrations. He has two other criminal cases against him.

Article Title: Andhra Pradesh deputy chief minister Pawan Kalyan and wife Anna Konidela announce separation
Article Text:
K Pawan Kalyan and his wife, Anna Konidela, announced their separation on Monday.





VIJAYAWADA: Andhra Pradesh deputy chief minister K Pawan Kalyan and his wife, Anna Konidela, announced their separation on Monday, after 13 years of marriage, in a joint statement. Pawan Kalyan and Anna confirmed their decision in a joint statement issued through the Jana Sena’s official WhatsApp media group.“After sharing a significant part of our lives, we have decided to part ways with mutual understanding and respect. Though our marriage has come to an end, we remain good friends and devoted parents to our wonderful children. Their happiness and well-being will always remain our shared priority. During this personal transition, we seek your understanding, kindness, and respect for our privacy. We extend our heartfelt gratitude to everyone who has stood by us throughout this journey,” the joint statement issued by Pawan Kalyan and Anna Konidela read.Pawan married Anna Konidela (née Lezhneva), a Russian national, in Sept 2013, following his divorce from actress Renu Desai in 2012. The couple have a daughter and a son. Anna also acted alongside Pawan Kalyan in his film Teen Maar.Pawan married his first wife, Nandini, in Sept 1997. The couple separated in 1999 and divorced in 2008. He subsequently married actress Renu Desai in 2009, and they have a daughter and a son together.
Article Summary: Andhra Pradesh deputy chief minister K Pawan Kalyan and his wife, Anna Konidela, announced their separation on Monday. The couple confirmed their decision in a joint statement issued through the Jana Sena’s official WhatsApp media group. “We remain good friends and devoted parents to our wonderful children,” the statement read.
